name: work.stillopen/jobs
title: StillOpen remote jobs
description: Remote jobs re-checked against each employer's own ATS, with evidence they're still open.

tools.name: search_jobs
tools.description: Find fully-remote job listings, each re-checked against the employer's own job board. Returns a summary record per role — no job descriptions, because twenty ads would fill your context with roles the reader did not choose. Call `get_job` for the ad once one looks worth reading. Every record carries `evidence_type` and `verified_at`: present those with the listing rather than asserting it is open.

q.description: free text over the title, the skills read from the ad, and the ad body

level.description: seniority, read from the title. `unspecified` is the 40% of titles that state none, which is not the same as mid

loc.description: an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (`de`), a macro region (`emea`), `worldwide` for roles with no stated restriction, or `unspecified`. A country answers 'can I apply from here', so it includes roles open across a region containing it and roles open worldwide; a record's `locations` may therefore not name the country

area.description: functional area, read from the title rather than from the employer's department field

company.description: a `company_slug` from any record. Not a company name — names collide, and several here belong to two unrelated employers

pay.description: minimum annual pay. Compared against the top of the published range in the currency published; nothing is converted, and a job board's estimate is excluded

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: One listing in full, including the employer's own ad. Use it after `search_jobs` rather than instead of it: this returns thousands of characters of advertisement. The id is the number in a listing URL — /job/9620-company-title is 9620. A listing that was folded into another answers under the id you asked for and reports `merged_into`.

tools.name: check_job_status
tools.description: Whether each of up to 100 listings is still open, and on what evidence — in one call. The most useful tool here: given a link to a role somebody is about to apply for, this is what separates a live posting from a filled one, with a date and a kind of evidence attached. A closed listing reports whether the closure was **observed** (a source was asked and said the posting was gone) or **inferred** (it aged out, which is a guess about the employer rather than an answer from one). This reads evidence already stored: it reports the result of our most recent check, and does not perform a live check against the employer's board at the moment you call it. Two dates come back and they answer different questions: **`verified_at`** is when we last asked the employer's system and it said yes, and it is the one to show a reader; `last_seen_at` is when a source last carried the posting, which happens far more often and is normally the newer of the two. `last_seen_at` being newer is ordinary, not a contradiction. **`status: unknown` means we have never held this id** — it is not-found, not un-checked. The value for 'nothing has proved it gone but no source has carried it lately' is `unconfirmed`.

tools.name: get_company_stats
tools.description: What one employer's listings on this site add up to: how many roles are open, where they hire, what they hire for, and what their listings disclose about pay. Takes a `company_slug` from any search record. Answers only for employers whose board identity we have confirmed, because a page asserting one company's vacancies under another company's name is the failure this gate exists to prevent.

tools.name: check_agent
tools.description: Check another agent before calling it. Given a domain, returns the open-source a2a-agent-checker's verdict on its A2A Agent Card (`/.well-known/agent-card.json`) and whether its endpoint answers a GetTask probe correctly, plus how many of the last 30 days it was reachable. Agents we already watch are answered from our daily log (`source: watch_log`); otherwise one live check is made (`source: live`): one card fetch and at most one GetTask per binding on the card's own host. It never sends the agent a message. A `fail` verdict means the card or endpoint breaks the A2A v1.0 spec, which includes agents still on the older 0.3 format.

domain.description: a domain such as example.com; a pasted URL is reduced to its host

tools.name: verify_job
tools.description: Is the job behind this URL still open? Takes a job URL from anywhere. A posting on an employer's ATS that we track is answered from our stored evidence (`matched_by: ats_posting`); any other URL is matched by the company and title in its words (`url_words`) and refused unless exactly one role fits. A URL naming neither, such as a LinkedIn job id, needs `company` and `title` (`company_title`). A supported ATS posting we do not track gets one live check of the employer's own board (`result: checked`, `evidence_type: ats_checked_once`): `not_listed` may also mean a mistyped URL, so never present it as closed. The page itself is never fetched unless it is the employer's ATS. Free allowance of 20 URLs a day per client address, shared with the HTTP endpoint.

company.description: the employer, if the URL does not name it

title.description: the job title, if the URL does not name it
